topic: Template Function Specialization and SFINAE for Type Traits
explanation: In modern C++, template specialization and SFINAE (Substitution Failure Is Not An Error) are techniques used to enable or disable template instantiations based on type traits or compile-time conditions. This allows writing highly generic and efficient code that adapts to different types, facilitating type-safe function overloading and customization without runtime overhead. These features are essential for creating flexible, type-aware libraries and components in C++.
code_example: // SFINAE example: only enable for integral types
// printIfIntegral(3.14); // Error: substitution failure, function not enabled for non-integral types
example_explanation: This example demonstrates how template specialization allows customizing behavior for specific types—in this case, an explicit specialization for 'int'. It also shows how SFINAE with 'std::enable_if' can restrict template instantiation to only integral types, enabling compile-time type-based function overloading. The code highlights modern C++ techniques for writing flexible, type-safe generic functions that adapt based on type traits, which is fundamental in template metaprogramming.
